provenance: SYNTHETIC. These scores were derived by applying the anchors in solutions/rubric.ts to each fixture's KNOWN defect list — they are not blind human judgements. See README.md for what that does and does not prove, and replace this file with real labels before trusting a judge in production.

labels.rationale: Faithful, container policy respected, no clarification needed, exact names. All four criteria met.

Missing `type` makes the output unparseable, so the system gets nothing — worse than a cosmetic naming lapse. Note the rubric has NO anchor for unparseable output: criteria 1-2 are technically met, which would argue for 3+. Labeled 2 on consequence. This is a genuine gap in the rubric, not in the model.

The ordered item and flavor are right, but a Cup the customer never mentioned appears alongside it. Hallucinated item fails criterion 1, so the hard cap applies. Not a 1, because the substance of the order is correct.

Espresso is right and the cancellation was understood; what remains is an empty container group. No hallucination (the cone WAS named), no clarification owed. The anchors do not cover an empty group either — labeled 3 as a structural defect with no customer-visible loss.
'Choco Scoop' does not resolve, so at runtime the scoop silently vanishes and the customer does not get what they ordered. That is anchor 2: an ordered item dropped without a clarification.
A standalone item placed inside a container group, and the Cup was never mentioned. Criterion 2 fails and a container was invented — anchor 2.
No container was named, so the model had to ask; instead it picked one. Anchor 2 literally: a container was invented.
The coke is right. The banana split is NOT on the menu, so criterion 1's 'dropped an on-menu item' does not strictly apply — but the off-menu rule demands a clarification and none came. Anchor 3.
The clarification is genuinely good and specific, but the output also sets Hazelnut, which is not in the Flavor group. Anchor 3: an option rule violated with criteria 1-2 intact.
Scoops and container are right. Caramel Sauce is not offered on a Cup, and the unavailable-extra rule requires a clarification that is missing. Both halves sit under anchor 3.
A Strawberry Scoop the customer never ordered. Anchor 1: hallucinated item, and the customer would be charged for it.
Exactly the policy: resolved item kept, container-less scoop withheld, one specific clarification asked.
Compound menu item matched instead of decomposed into scoop + container. All criteria met.
